prompt: One coherent photographic garden space containing exactly one Huagang Guanyu imperial stele pavilion at West Lake, Hangzhou. All six images depict different views and details of this SAME pavilion, not six different buildings: front real photograph, left oblique, right oblique, back, overhead roof and close detail. Reconstruct a single shared pavilion with one upturned grey tiled roof, four pale stone columns, carved brown wooden brackets and dark railing enclosing one stone stele. Keep the red inscription on the front face only; the rear face is plain stone. Use the overhead image to constrain the same roof, not as a separate ground-level view. Preserve the pond and winter garden trees. Keep a coherent flat pebble-paved walking area in front, to both sides and behind the pavilion so the camera can walk around the same building. Maintain realistic scale and consistent roof, columns, railing and stele across views. No additional pavilions, no duplicated monuments, no floating roofs, no people. The first view is a real photo; the other five are AI-inferred references. This is a visual consistency experiment, not a surveyed reconstruction.

comparison.purpose: Qualitative six-view trial; not a controlled benchmark. The prompt, crop, stochastic generation and reference set differ.
